# Performance & Timing

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `performance.*` can be implemented with a single `clock_gettime()` call. Includes `Date`, since real JS/Node group wall-clock timing APIs together too.

**Coverage**: 11/12 (~92%) · **Strict Coverage**: 6/12 (50%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `performance.now()` | ✅ | | • Milliseconds since the program's **time origin** (process start), as a `double` (sub-millisecond precision) — the origin is captured once at process start by an `llvm.global_ctors` constructor, matching the spec's origin-relative reading ([ADR-00568](../adr/ADR-00568.md))<br>• Monotonic (`CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW` on macOS, nanosecond-grained like libuv's `uv_hrtime`; `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux) — unlike `Date.now()`, not tied to wall-clock time ([ADR-01270](../adr/ADR-01270.md))<br>• See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md) |
| `performance.mark` / `measure` / `getEntries*` / `clearMarks` / `clearMeasures` / `timerify` / `timeOrigin` | ✅ | | • User-timing entries as Node v24 keeps them: `mark()` returns a `PerformanceMark` (its `detail` structured-cloned), `measure(name, start?, end?)` or `measure(name, options)` returns a `PerformanceMeasure`; a missing mark throws a `SyntaxError` `DOMException`<br>• Written in TypeScript: `lib/node/perf_hooks.ts` ([ADR-01265](../adr/ADR-01265.md)) |
| `Date` | ✅ | • `toString`'s zone name comes from a built-in table of the common zones' abbreviations; a zone outside it prints the C library's abbreviation (`GMT-0300 (-03)` where Node says `(Brasilia Standard Time)`) | • Local time is not implemented: every local getter, the component constructor and `toString` work in UTC<br>• `new Date()` / `new Date(ms)` / `new Date(isoString)` (the string form parses via the same logic as `Date.parse`, including its `-1`-on-unparseable sentinel — see [ADR-00038](../adr/ADR-00038.md)) / `new Date(year, month, day?, hours?, minutes?, seconds?, ms?)` (month 0-indexed, matching `getMonth()`; omitted trailing fields default like real JS — day to 1, everything after that to 0; see [ADR-00039](../adr/ADR-00039.md))<br>• `getFullYear/Month/Date/Day/Hours/Minutes/Seconds/Milliseconds` (+ the `set*` setters), `getTime`/`valueOf`, `toISOString`<br>• The `getUTC*`/`setUTC*` accessors alias the field getters/setters — since the stored timestamp is UTC, these are fully faithful to Node's UTC methods (unlike the local `get*`/`set*`, which carry the UTC deviation above) ([ADR-00844](../adr/ADR-00844.md))<br>• See [ADR-00014](../adr/ADR-00014.md)<br>• Local time follows the host's time zone, as Node's does: the local getters, the component constructor, the local setters, `toString` (`GMT+0300 (Eastern European Summer Time)`), `toDateString` and `getTimezoneOffset`; `Date.UTC` and the `getUTC*`/`setUTC*` accessors are UTC. An unparseable string or a `NaN` time value is an Invalid Date: `getTime()` is `NaN`, `toString()` is `Invalid Date`, `toISOString()` throws a `RangeError` and JSON gives `null` ([ADR-01315](../adr/ADR-01315.md)) |
| `Date.now()` | ✅ | | • Milliseconds since epoch, via `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, ...)` |
| `Date.parse(string)` | ✅ | | • ISO 8601 strings, with or without milliseconds: `Z` (UTC), a `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` timezone offset (converted to UTC), or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date<br>• See [ADR-00015](../adr/ADR-00015.md) and [ADR-00017](../adr/ADR-00017.md)<br>• The ECMAScript date-time format (a date-only form is UTC, a date-time without an offset local time) and V8's legacy forms (`toString`/`toUTCString` output, `Jul 15 2024`, `2024/07/15 10:30`); unparseable input is `NaN` ([ADR-01315](../adr/ADR-01315.md)) |
| `Date` setters (`setFullYear`, `setMonth`, `setDate`, `setHours`, `setMinutes`, `setSeconds`, `setMilliseconds`, `setTime`) | ✅ | • Requires a named-variable receiver (not a field access or call result — this compiler's Date is a plain number, not a reference object, so there's no heap location to mutate otherwise) | • Mutate a named Date variable in place and return the new timestamp, matching real JS<br>• See [ADR-00016](../adr/ADR-00016.md)<br>• Multi-argument setter overloads cascade into the following fields (`setFullYear(y, m, d)`, `setHours(h, m, s, ms)`, …) ([ADR-00488](../adr/ADR-00488.md)) |
| `Date` arithmetic (`date ± durationMs`, `date - date`, `date += durationMs`) | ✅ | • Under `-compat=js`, a compound `date += n` / `date -= n` keeps the variable a Date; JavaScript turns it into a string / a number (the plain `+`/`-` do) | • The strict lane rejects arithmetic on a Date as TypeScript does (TS2362, TS2363, TS2365): the millisecond count is `getTime()` ([ADR-01134](../adr/ADR-01134.md))<br>• Under `-compat=js`, `date + x` concatenates the date string and `date - x` (`*`, `/`, `%`, `**`, the relational operators) reads its millisecond count, as JavaScript does ([ADR-01310](../adr/ADR-01310.md))<br>• See [ADR-00018](../adr/ADR-00018.md) |
| `Date.prototype.toDateString()` | ✅ | | • Fixed `"Www Mon DD YYYY"` shape (e.g. `"Thu Jan 01 1970"`), matching real JS exactly except for the UTC deviation<br>• See [ADR-00019](../adr/ADR-00019.md) |
| `Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString()` | ✅ | • One fixed `"M/D/YYYY"` format (the default en-US shape) in local time; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support | • See [ADR-00019](../adr/ADR-00019.md) |
| `PerformanceObserver` | ✅ | | • `observe({ entryTypes })` / `observe({ type, buffered })`, `disconnect()`, `takeRecords()`, `supportedEntryTypes`; entries arrive on a later turn of the loop, sorted by start time ([ADR-01265](../adr/ADR-01265.md)) |
| `createHistogram` / `monitorEventLoopDelay` | ✅ | • A histogram keeps exact samples, not Node's HDR histogram (3 significant figures): a percentile of large values can differ in its last digits | • `RecordableHistogram` (`record`, `recordDelta`, `add`) and the event-loop-delay `IntervalHistogram` (`enable`/`disable`), with `min`/`max`/`mean`/`stddev`/`percentile(s)` and their BigInt forms ([ADR-01265](../adr/ADR-01265.md)) |
| `performance.eventLoopUtilization` / `performance.nodeTiming` | ❌ | | • Not ported from Node's `lib/internal/perf` |
